title: SimCHW: ABrowser-Based, Multi-Modal AI Simulation Platform for Community Health Worker Communication Training
content: Community Health Workers (CHWs) are frontline agents of health equity, yet scalable, psychologically safe training in trauma-informed communication remains scarce. Standardized patient (SP) role-play—the gold standard—is costly, logistically constrained, and difficult to repeat. We present SimCHW, an open, browser-based simulation platform that couples large language model (LLM) patient personas with real-time speech recognition and synthesis, a three-dimensional emotional state model (anxiety, defensiveness, openness), a transparent rule-based scoring rubric across four CHW competencies (Communication, Empathy, Assessment, Support), and a multi-user instructor dashboard. Two iterative front-end implementations are described and compared. We report a heuristic evaluation of the scoring layer and identify a critical validity gap: keyword-based rubrics detect surface empathy markers but fail to credit paraphrased empathy, penalize judgmental language, or capture open-ended assessment questions. We argue that SimCHW is best positioned as a design artifact and testbed for a new class of LLM-assisted competency rubrics, and we outline a rigorous mixed-methods evaluation agenda. The platform’s modular, standards-aware architecture (SCORM hooks, FHIR-inspired patient input, WebSocket avatar bridge) lowers the barrier to adoption across community college, FQHC, and public-health training contexts.
